conclusion: B2 CLOSED on the owned tests at baseline binary 157748a. The GitFS stage-cleanup job is proven to run concurrently with a real native push that itself holds the repository data lease (rootyard-data-v1 ShareLock, application_name=rootyard, xact-scoped), cannot delete the 4000 staged temps while that lease is held, and succeeds only after the push publishes. 39 and 40 stay PENDING combined integration only.

delta.note: tests-only commit; production identity remains certified compile cb8d1b9 / inputs 0f865a

b2_closure.previous_gap: The earlier barrier was a test-held shared advisory lock, so native publication was not itself the data-lease holder.
b2_closure.new_method: The fixture holds ONLY the product ref key rootyard-ref-v1:<repo>:<ref> via a session-level try lock. The real native HTTP push takes read_leases::shared on rootyard-data-v1 first (src/storage/ref_publication.rs:270, entry at src/git_http.rs:204) and then retries the exact-ref lock, so the data-lease holder is the application backend waiting on that ref key. No hook wrapping and no product change.

evidence.exclusive_probe: pg_try_advisory_lock on the rootyard-data-v1 key returned false while the native lease was held

why_sound: pg_locks filter requires locktype=advisory, granted, mode=ShareLock and objsubid=1, which selects the single-bigint advisory-key namespace (objsubid=2 is the two-int key namespace); objsubid does not distinguish transaction from session scope. The holder is established instead by the exact rootyard-data-v1 key, application_name=rootyard, the fixture pid being excluded, and five stable consecutive samples.
application_name=rootyard is set on the application pool (src/db.rs:18), and the fixture is excluded by pid, by application_name and by native_pid != fixture_pid.
Five consecutive samples at 50 ms spacing inside a 2.15 s push window, so this is sustained holding, not a transient blip.

read_leases::exclusive retries every 50 ms until its deadline (src/storage/read_leases.rs:81-110), so the maintenance worker stays claimed and denied for as long as the native shared lease is held and cannot reach gitfs::execute (src/storage_lifecycle/worker.rs:51).

Direct behavioural proof, not only a probe: the job was running while 4000 aged .tmp-* files still existed and were asserted present; after the fixture released the ref key the push completed rc 0, the job succeeded, deleted 4000, and completed after push end.

Cleanup scope is unchanged: gitfs_stage_cleanup only removes aged .tmp-<uuid> files under lfs/<repo> (src/storage_lifecycle/gitfs.rs), so committed <oid> bytes are never candidates; the LFS row and bytes were re-verified ready and identical afterwards.

correction_to_prior_review.item: Prior finding F1 (remote hydration writing straight to the final oid path, possible partial-file exposure) is RETRACTED as a false concern.
correction_to_prior_review.basis: src/storage/remote_objects.rs get_to_file writes to a sibling .rootyard-object-<uuid> temp, enforces size and sha256 against the key digest, sync_all, then fs::rename onto the destination and fsyncs the parent; the temp is removed on failure. The caller fs::set_permissions(0600) after a completed rename cannot truncate it.
correction_to_prior_review.residual_noted: In-process failures clean the temp, but a hard crash can leave a .rootyard-object-<uuid> file in lfs/<repo>/ while gitfs_stage_cleanup only reclaims names matching .tmp-<uuid> (src/storage_lifecycle/gitfs.rs). Harmless for retention and never confusable with a committed <oid> path, but a tiny housekeeping residual if the prefix is not widened.

accepted_supported_mode_residuals: Loopback single host, local data volume and local Garage on a second data directory; no vendor credentials or hardware are required or claimed.
The barrier fixture needs the psql client and a dedicated disposable database; environment-specific and passed in gc17.
No LFS delete or GC API exists; retention is asserted through failed, duplicate and interrupted uploads, permission removal and the stage-cleanup job.
Non-LFS compatibility push uses 300 small files against 4096 small-blob and 20000 object bounds.
Documentation claiming older manifest formats need the legacy binary is untested.
restored_schema_versions_verified remains a constant true; the real evidence is manifest schema_versions plus the restore-path assertion.
gitfs_stage_cleanup deletes at most 4096 entries per run, so more than 4096 stale temps need repeated runs.
